fields.display_title: Official Review of Paper371 by Reviewer Geje
fields.replying_to: Replying to Rethinking skip connection model as a learnable Markov chain

fields.display_title: Q1: Central claims of the paper are not clear: Consider the “inefficient” Markov chain in Fig 2 (a). Both the inefficient and efficient Markov chains successfully convert data from the source to the target domain. In fact, for a classification-type model, there should be no difference in the final test accuracies of both efficient and inefficient models. If learning an efficient Markov chain is hard, it is not clear what is the advantage of an efficient Markov chain.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper371 by Reviewer Geje

fields.display_title: Q2: In Proof 2.3, the paper derives only a c value for $\epsilon$. What is the quality of the approximation? Are there any upper bounds to the absolute error? This is important because the approximation has a direct impact on the quality of the proposed regularizer. (The steps in Proof 2.3 should be numbered).
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper371 by Reviewer Geje

fields.display_title: Q3: It is not clear if a higher value of $\epsilon$ leads to a better model. The paper should show better evidence for this.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper371 by Reviewer Geje

fields.display_title: Q4:In Fig 4 (b) the difference in $\epsilon$ between the two models is minimal. In fact, the value of $\epsilon$ peaks early in training, but is not accompanied by peak accuracy.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper371 by Reviewer Geje

fields.display_title: Q5: The paper should also consider including additional state-of-the-art baselines for the machine translation task, as currently only the plain Transformer is considered.
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper371 by Reviewer Geje
